One lab-grown carat, three published prices this week: $711, $650, $511.

CaratRadar's asking-price average, republished this morning, reads $711. TheDiamondPrice's fair-market estimate for August puts it at $650, inside a $590 to $760 range. A third page this desk carried on 7 August, StoneAlgo, read $511. Span: about 39%.

The two read today aren't actually in conflict — $711 sits inside TheDiamondPrice's own band, above its $675 midpoint. One measures what sellers ask. The other estimates what stones sell for. Neither page publishes the distance between the two as a number, so a jeweller reading either has no way to know which side of the trade it describes.

This matters because lab-grown took 61% of US engagement centre stones in 2025 — the single most-bought diamond in America, and the one with no settled price. Natural goods have the Rapaport list. Grown goods have a handful of aggregators, each computing something different, none clearing a market.

Our own wire tape moves with this edition: the lab-grown line now carries $711, sourced and dated, replacing an unsourced $727 that sat there for days.

The AED 10.44 gap between two Dubai gold pages isn't closing — and that's the story.

Kitco's 6am spot this morning: $4,372.80 an ounce, or AED 516.31 a gram at the dirham's fixed peg, both this desk's arithmetic. LivePriceOfGold's board reads AED 516.26 — five fils from the peg. Goodreturns reads AED 526.75 — a gap of AED 10.44, or 2.02% of the metal.

All three readings moved almost in lockstep overnight: the peg figure added AED 3.72, LivePriceOfGold added AED 3.81, Goodreturns added AED 3.50. That's the finding. This paper flagged a AED 13.25 step in one of these pages on 8 August against a metal move of only AED 3.13. Three sessions later, the wedge it opened has held at roughly AED 10.5 through a metal rally. A margin that arrives in one move and then tracks the market afterward is a pricing decision, not a data lag.

A jeweller now has a number to plan around: quote the peg arithmetic beside whatever page you use, and watch for the wedge to move again — that's the event, not the daily print.

Kalyan Jewellers, a national chain with more than 400 showrooms across seven countries, is launching a brand that will trade in exactly one Indian state.

Akshaya Thanga Maligai opens its first store at Panagal Park in Chennai on 21 August, selling hallmarked gold and certified diamonds cut to Tamil Nadu design preferences, fronted by actor Sivakarthikeyan. Kalyan plans to expand it by franchise within the state before considering anywhere else.

The tell is the financing. Franchising puts the working capital for the gold on somebody else's balance sheet, at a moment when the metal is the most expensive it has ever been — spot at $4,372.80 an ounce this morning. And the demand backdrop isn't a growth story: India's gold jewellery demand fell 15% by weight last quarter, the weakest since the pandemic, while Kalyan itself took over 46% of its June-quarter revenue in recycled metal.

Read plainly: Kalyan is admitting its own name has a ceiling in a market it already trades in, and paying to get under that ceiling with a purpose-built local brand backed by national buying power. For independents in Tamil Nadu, that's the harder competitor to see coming.
